diagram_candidates.certainty: Editorial candidate; the two differentials, totalization, augmented row/column, and quasi-isomorphism maps are all explicit in the ItemBody.
diagram_candidates.excerpt: The ItemBody defines D^{p,q}=C^p(U,G^q), horizontal Čech differential h, vertical Godement differential v with hv=vh, total differential h+(-1)^p v, an augmented global-sections column Γ(X,G^q), and maps u and w into Tot D; it proves augmented rows exact, columns acyclic in positive degrees under the cover hypothesis, and u (and conditionally w) are quasi-isomorphisms.
diagram_candidates.maps_and_check: If drawn, place D^{p,q} on a first-quadrant grid with h:D^{p,q}→D^{p+1,q} pointing horizontally and v:D^{p,q}→D^{p,q+1} vertically; mark hv=vh and label Tot differential d=h+(-1)^p v. Show the augmented column at p=-1 as Γ(X,G^q)→D^{0,q} by restrictions s↦(s|_{U_i})_i. The extra row E^{p,-1}=C^p(U,F) maps vertically to D^{p,0} through ε:F→G^0. Distinguish the resulting cochain maps u:Γ(X,G•)→Tot D and w:C•(U,F)→Tot D. A diagram must keep the source indexing p,q, include the sign only in the total differential, and represent w as the extra row inclusion; exactness/quasi-isomorphism claims remain proved in text.
diagram_candidates.reason: The theorem is organized around row and column acyclicity of an explicit double complex and its totalization. A labelled grid makes the two directions, augmentation, and two comparison maps easier to follow without replacing the proof.

diagram_candidates.certainty: Editorial candidate; the finite map and every branch/fibre count are stated and computed explicitly.
diagram_candidates.excerpt: For algebraically closed k of characteristic not 2 and squarefree f of degree 2g+1 or 2g+2, the smooth projective model C of y²=f(x) maps finitely and surjectively by π:C→P¹_k with degree two. Its branch locus is the roots of f and additionally infinity when deg f is odd; each branch point has one preimage above it with e=2, and all other closed points have two points above them with e=1.
diagram_candidates.maps_and_check: Draw π:C→P¹_k as a degree-two morphism. Mark the n roots of f on the target, plus ∞ exactly when n is odd. Over each marked branch point show a single preimage with ramification index 2; over every unmarked closed point show two preimages, each index 1. For even n, infinity has two unramified preimages; for odd n, infinity is a branch point with one preimage of index 2. The count is n+[n odd]=2g+2 branch points in either parity case. Keep the hypotheses char(k)≠2, squarefreeness, algebraic closure, and n=2g+1 or 2g+2 visible; the schematic fibres reflect the statement and are not a proof of ramification.
diagram_candidates.reason: A degree-two cover with a parity-dependent branch point at infinity is a classic geometric relationship whose fibre and ramification data are central to this example. One schematic can expose the parity case and branch count at a glance.
